text: RWB-E1-032 is split and the secondary slice RWB-S9-E1032-APP is built on the rwb-partner frame: schema rwb_partner, base /api/recovery/partner/v1, topic rwb.partner.events.v1, queue rwb-partner, package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner.
why: No source states a partner slice or its frame; the split plan and the work package place the slice in S9 and Template R4 fixes the naming for every service.
read: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.2; _work/msr/context/S9.md; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json
impact: Sections 1, 12 and 13 use the S9 paths, topic and schema; a different frame would rewrite them.

text: The partner file channel of the OCR intake is this service's: a submission row in rwb_partner, one PartnerDocumentSubmitted fact carrying the instruction's case ID, the attach event consumed and the item read used to copy the match state; the match, the store and the held-item resolution stay with rwb-document.
why: No source states the boundary, and without it a partner file whose instruction is clear is held as an anonymous scan.
read: FSD S9 A2.5 and Screens; TSD S9 T5.1 and T5.3; legacy RWB-E1-032 sections 1, 2, 4 and 19
impact: Defines sections 1, 4, 9 and 12.4; the document hub keeps the document, the intake item and the review queue.

text: The story stays in wave 1 and its release is copied unchanged as 30 November 2026 (tentative), although rwb-partner is wave 4 in Arch v5.
why: R5.6 keeps the earlier W-MAP wave and R1 U7 keeps every date tentative and unchanged; a date is never raised as a gap.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 and R1 U7; _work/msr/context/S9.md service row
impact: The wave 1 entry check must have the S9 frame and its platform baseline available.

text: The H list stays empty as the work package fixes it and the seven platform CON rows of the DP table are treated as the wave-0 shared baseline of the service template, recorded in section 13 instead of as build dependencies.
why: The work package and the plan both carry H [], while the DP table adds a platform H row for each applied pattern.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R5.7; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json
impact: Ready to start stays Day 1; the platform rows are a wave-0 precondition, not an in-lane wait.

text: The two document operations, the intake creation call, the PartnerDocumentSubmitted payload and the 404 and 409 bodies are this story's design choice and are published by the S9 contract baseline and the P5 contract before Done.
why: No source names them and the story cannot be built without a shape.
read: TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2; _work/msr/context/S9.md Events; legacy RWB-E1-032 section 12
impact: Sections 12.1 to 12.4 and 12.8 rest on these shapes; a published change rewrites the tables, not the behaviour.

text: The intake bound, the acceptance decision code and its version, LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-INSTR-STATUS are reference values in force read at their version; where no source names one the story writes the placeholder and invents no value.
why: Every value a business person may change is versioned reference data (Template and Rules R3 default rulings; FSD S9 BR-S9-005) and no source fixes these names.
read: legacy RWB-E1-032 sections 3 and 8; TSD S9 T3.2; FSD S9 A2.5
impact: Section 13 configuration and section 14 rest on rows that must exist before the story is Done.

text: partner_intake is created by this story in rwb_partner with the columns listed in section 11, the standard audit columns and version, a unique key on instruction and file hash, and a partial index over the PENDING rows.
why: No data model carries a partner-side submission row and the state must be durable for the reconcile run and the partner read.
read: TSD S9 T3.0 and T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-032 section 11
impact: Sections 11, 12.7 and 13 define one new table; no foreign key leaves the schema.

text: All fifteen legacy criteria and the seventeen legacy test cases stay word for word with RWB-P5-E1032-APP; this slice owns no legacy criterion and writes AC1 to AC7 as new criteria with TC-S9-E1032-APP-01 to -08.
why: The legacy criteria test the matcher, the store and the reviewer, none of which this service performs.
impact: The RTM counts each legacy criterion once, against the primary slice; no legacy test is executed here.

text: The partner submission is reached from one of PRT-01 to PRT-04, most likely PRT-02 Instruction, and the screen number is left open until the partner portal screens are specified.
why: The FSD lists the four partner screens without naming the document submission.
impact: Section 15 names the service answer only; the screen work is the partner portal story's.

text: FSD S9 v3 and TSD S9 v2 are In review and not approved; the story proceeds as Draft (realignment v1) with no approval stop and no status change to the sources.
why: The D-RCV-60 overlay removes human approval gates and requires the work to continue on the sources as they stand.
read: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 Document control (Status In review); Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2 Document control (Status In review)
impact: The story is Draft; a later approval of the FSD or TSD may change the business rules it copies.
